summary: Requested read-only review and observed native specialist workflow pass: all three release blockers are evidenced and no unsupported interoperability claim is made. Overall frozen-rubric status is partial solely because strict capability isolation is unverified. This is successful review of a failing gateway, not successful gateway validation.

independence.method: Read frozen criteria, workflow, fixture and raw native traces; compared 68 baseline files and independently reran only local probe. No model execution or raw artifact edits.

criteria.finding: Installed workflow wrapper/body and relevant skills were actually read. Native metadata identifies tal-mcp and tal-consistency children with inherited model/reasoning; both completed substantive role-specific investigations.

Review-only mode was preserved, with no implementation owner needed for unchanged files. Independent MCP and consistency specialists examined distinct contract/enforcement questions against gateway digest f9e0ed88ef78f4621747421d7767e2b1afc5e357f9a81751bda35a32b3fd6a43. Main-session local probes corroborated findings, candidate hashes were checked, and the final synthesis retained both findings and limits.

All 68 baseline files match and no files were added, including every supplied input and installed dependency. No forbidden evaluator/repository access or external mutation is observed. Strict read/tool confinement remains unverified under documented runner capability deviations; case_compliant=false is preserved. Unused broad read capability is not an actual scope breach.

Final answer clearly labels direct Python adapter observations, unavailable mcp package and unexecuted HTTP/SDK peers. Synthetic verified-principal strings are not presented as credential verification. Missing SDK is an evidence gap rather than a new implementation defect; release remains blocked on concrete findings and required real-peer checks.

Separately identifies warm handle-only cache lookup before authorization and cold-path claimedPrincipal override. Supplied probe and isolated schedules reproduce Bob receiving Alice-private by each path; consistency reviewer confirms symmetric cold-outsider/owner-warm/warm-outsider history. Recommended authority remains verified_principal, with authorization before cached return.

Finds method header/body disagreement reaching application dispatch and extends local checks to name/version mismatches and missing metadata. Explicitly preserves MCP 2026-07-28 per-request metadata, excludes legacy initialization/session requirements, and recommends rejection before dispatch with zero dispatch delta and no payload.

Names specification 2026-07-28 and commit pin, Python mcp 2.2.0, Python >=3.10 and intended Streamable HTTP. Distinguishes expected local dictionary return from SDK tool-result packaging and specifies missing actual peer, authentication, capability, error-layer and interruption checks.
